citations.quote: The primary efficacy study CACZ885D2304 (D2304) only evaluated patients diagnosed with MWS, while two open-label studies, CACZ885A2102 (A2102) and CACZ885D2306 (D2306), evaluated patients diagnosed with MWS, FCAS, NOMID, MWS/NOMID.

design.text: Three-part study: Part 1 was an 8-week open-label single-dose run-in to identify responders; responders who did not relapse by Week 8 entered Part 2, a 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled withdrawal phase; followed by Part 3 open-label treatment.

citations.quote: This was a three-part study where Part 1 was an eight week open-label, active treatment, single dose, run-in phase to identify patients that responded to treatment. Only those patients that responded to treatment in Part 1 and did not relapse by Week 8, entered Part 2, a 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, withdrawal phase.

population.text: Patients 9 to 74 years of age with the Muckle-Wells Syndrome (MWS) phenotype of CAPS.

citations.quote: The efficacy and safety of ILARIS for the treatment of CAPS was demonstrated in Study 1, a 3-part trial in patients 9 to 74 years of age with the MWS phenotype of CAPS.

endpoint.text: Primary efficacy endpoint in the withdrawal period (Part 2) was the proportion of patients that had a disease flare (disease relapse or discontinuation prior to completing Part 2).

citations.quote: In the withdrawal period of the pivotal efficacy study, D2304, the primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients that had a disease flare. A flare was defined as either a disease relapse or discontinued prior to completing Part 2.

n.text: 35 patients enrolled in Part 1; 31 complete responders randomized into Part 2 (16 placebo, 15 Ilaris).

citations.quote: This study screened 41 patients of which 35 were enrolled into Part 1. Of these 35 patients, 31 achieved a complete response and were randomized into Part 2. Sixteen patients were randomized to placebo, and 15 patients were randomized to Ilaris.

result.text: No disease flares in the Ilaris group (0 of 15), vs 13 of 16 (81%) in placebo; odds ratio 0, p < 0.01.

target_moa.text: Canakinumab is a recombinant human monoclonal anti-human IL-1β antibody of the IgG1κ isotype that antagonizes IL-1β by binding it and interfering with its interaction with the IL-1 receptor; uncontrolled overproduction of IL-1 is the pathogenetic mechanism of CAPS inflammation.

citations.quote: Canakinumab is a recombinant human monoclonal anti-human interleukin-1\beta (IL-1\beta) antibody of the IgG1\kappa isotype. The drug product, Ilaris, antagonizes the activity of human IL-1\beta by binding with it and thus interfering with the ability of the cytokine to interact with its receptor.
Uncontrolled overproduction of IL-1 is thought to be the pathogenetic mechanism for the resulting inflammation seen in CAPS patients.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions are nasopharyngitis, diarrhea, influenza, headache and nausea. Injection site reactions occurred in 9% of patients in Part 1. Most serious risk is an increased risk of serious infections.

description.text: Expanded indication to include adults with active Adult-Onset Still's Disease (AOSD)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for expansion of the approved indication for the treatment of Active Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (SJIA) in patients aged 2 years and older, to include the new population of patients with active Adult-Onset Still's Disease (AOSD). Both, SJIA and AOSD, are referred to as Still's Disease. With the approval of this Prior Approval supplemental biologics application, canakinumab is indicated for the treatment of active Still's Disease, including AOSD and SJIA in patients aged 2 years and older.
